title: Reactions of alcohols
log: 2026-10-27T00:53:11Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Reactions of alcohols
card: Alcohols burn in plenty of oxygen to make carbon dioxide and water. The reaction releases energy, so alcohols such as ethanol can be used as fuels.
With heat and a concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, an alcohol can lose water to form an alkene. For example, ethanol gives ethene.
An oxidising agent such as acidified dichromate can oxidise an alcohol. A primary alcohol forms an aldehyde, and with further oxidation a carboxylic acid.
A secondary alcohol is oxidised to a ketone. A tertiary alcohol is not oxidised under these conditions, because its carbon with the OH group has no hydrogen atom to lose.
draft.remember: Type decides oxidation: primary gives aldehyde then acid, secondary gives ketone, tertiary stays unchanged.

a.q: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. It is heated with acidified dichromate. What is the main organic product?
a.why: A secondary alcohol is oxidised to a ketone. An aldehyde and then an acid form only from a primary alcohol, so those options are wrong. Reaction does occur, because the carbon with the OH group has a hydrogen atom to lose.
a.clue: Think about which type of alcohol propan-2-ol is.

b.q: Three alcohol samples are each heated with acidified dichromate. Sample X is primary, Y is secondary and Z is tertiary. Which result is correct?
opts: Only Y gives a ketone and an acid
X and Z are oxidised but Y is not
b.why: A tertiary alcohol has no hydrogen on the carbon with the OH group, so Z is not oxidised. X and Y are both oxidised, so the claim that only X reacts is wrong. Y gives a ketone, not an acid, and X gives an aldehyde or acid.
b.clue: Which type has no hydrogen on the carbon bonded to OH?
